sources.content:
# Banking Agent Harness

A Python banking assistant that separates language-model suggestions from transfer authorization. The model can look up an account or propose a transfer; application code validates the proposal, requires confirmation in a later user turn, and records the simulated outcome.

[Live demo](https://banking-agent-harness.vercel.app) · [Tests](https://github.com/harshgavandit/banking-agent-harness/actions/workflows/tests.yml) · [Hosted verification](verification/VERCEL-DEPLOYMENT.md)

**Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, Google ADK, LiteLLM, OpenAI, Upstash Redis, Vercel.

![A confirmed simulated transfer with its resulting account balance](verification/browser-confirmed-transfer.jpg)

## Try the workflow

```text
What is my savings account balance?
Transfer 1000 rupees to Aaron.
confirm
Check transaction TXN001.
```

- Check balance, daily transfer allowance, and existing transactions.
- Find beneficiaries by name, ID, or the last four account digits. Ambiguous matches require a choice; blocked beneficiaries are rejected.
- Review recipient and amount before approving a staged transfer in a separate message or with **Confirm transfer**.
- Refresh the page and continue the same demo session. Other visitors receive separate accounts and histories.

All accounts and transactions use mock data. No real money moves.

## How a transfer runs

```text
Browser + signed session cookie
  → FastAPI: origin / payload checks + Redis session lease
  → ADK agent: bounded model/tool calls
  → Deterministic policy: beneficiary, balance, amount, daily allowance
  → Pending proposal: no debit until a later explicit confirmation
  → Revalidate → simulated executor → recorded transaction outcome
  → Atomic Redis snapshot commit → updated account and tool results
```

The important boundaries live in code:

| Decision | Implementation |
| --- | --- |
| Transfer eligibility | [`policy_service.py`](app/services/policy_service.py) checks finite positive amounts, beneficiary status, balance, and allowance independently of the prompt. |
| Confirmation | [`banking_tools.py`](app/tools/banking_tools.py) requires a previously staged proposal and an explicit confirmation from a different invocation. It expires old proposals and revalidates before execution. |
| Actual outcome | [`transaction_executor.py`](app/services/transaction_executor.py) supplies `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, or `PENDING`. Failed transfers leave the balance unchanged; pending transfers hold funds. |
| Visitor isolation | [`hosted_store.py`](app/hosted_store.py) keeps one Redis snapshot per visitor with a 120-second lease, compare-owner commit, and 24-hour inactivity expiry. |
| Bounded execution | [`agent.py`](app/agent.py) applies Redis user/model admission and tool limits. The hosted runner bounds each turn to 75 seconds and eight model calls. |
| Request boundary | [`web.py`](app/web.py) validates declared lengths and caps actual streamed POST bodies at 12,000 bytes before parsing or calling a handler. Missing, chunked or falsely small length headers cannot bypass the byte limit. Error responses retain the API's no-store and browser security headers. |

## Run locally

Use Python 3.12. From the repository root:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.lock.txt
Copy-Item app/.env.example app/.env
```

On macOS/Linux, activate with `source .venv/bin/activate` and copy with `cp app/.env.example app/.env`. Set values in the untracked `app/.env`:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Server-side OpenAI credential. |
| `LLM_MODEL` | LiteLLM model identifier; default `openai/gpt-4o-mini`. |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` | Required for the public-style app's snapshot storage and for enabled admission limits. |
| `DEMO_SESSION_SECRET` | Random signing secret of at least 32 characters for the public-style app's cookie. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | Set `true` to enforce the Redis limits; Redis failures then block agent execution. |
| `MOCK_TRANSACTION_OUTCOME` | Optional `SUCCESS`, `FAILED`, or `PENDING` to exercise different results. |

See [`app/.env.example`](app/.env.example) for timeouts, request limits, and tool/transfer budgets. Keep credentials server-side.

Run the same FastAPI interface used by the deployment:

```powershell
python -m uvicorn app.web:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8011
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8011>. The original local ADK developer interface is also available with `python scripts/serve.py --port 8010` or `./start.ps1`; its in-memory sessions are separate from the Redis-backed web app. The developer interface is not mounted on the public deployment.

## Tests and reproducible checks

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
python -m pip check
python -m compileall -q app scripts tests index.py
node --check web/app.js
```

The offline suite covers policy rejection, later-turn confirmation, execution outcomes, visitor isolation, signed cookies, cross-origin rejection, overlapping turns, and actual ASGI body limits. Request-boundary tests include malformed and duplicate lengths, zero-prefixed length overflow, chunked input, false length claims and exact-limit byte preservation. GitHub Actions runs it on Windows and Linux with Python 3.12; tests use doubles rather than paid provider requests.

With the local web app running and credentials configured, `python scripts/verify_hosted.py http://127.0.0.1:8011` exercises real model calls, restored proposals, and separate visitor accounts. It consumes provider quota and changes only synthetic demo account state. The separate `scripts/verify_live.py` and `scripts/verify_http.py` check the agent and ADK developer interface.

The [20 October hosted report](verification/VERCEL-DEPLOYMENT.md) records the deployment checks and their limits. It is a dated observation, not a load-capacity or banking-compliance claim.

## Scope

This is an anonymous-session engineering demonstration, without identity-verified accounts or payment rails. Snapshot expiry resets the demo; the daily allowance is a session budget without a midnight reset. Redis serialization protects this mock ledger, not an external financial transaction. Real banking would additionally require durable financial ledgers, authenticated identities, reconciliation, and operational controls.

# Symposium RAG Bot — Shared Semantic Cache

A PDF question-answering application with page citations, exact and semantic answer reuse, and Redis request admission. The hosted FastAPI app shares a bounded cache across serverless instances; local development also supports SQLite and Valkey cache adapters.

[Live demo](https://symposium-rag-bot.vercel.app) · [Tests](https://github.com/harshgavandit/RAG-Semantic-Cache-Symposium-Bot/actions/workflows/tests.yml) · [Workload and recovery evidence](benchmarks/README.md)

**Stack:** Python 3.12, FastAPI, OpenAI, LangChain, FAISS, Upstash Redis, SQLite/Valkey, Streamlit, Vercel.

![The hosted chatbot showing its answer and document reference](evidence/vercel-desktop.jpg)

sources.content:
## What to explore

Ask about the date, venue, schedule, eligibility, competitions, or registration fees. Answers include page references; the interface also shows when an answer came from cache. The public demo uses a **fictional Innovate 2026 guide**, not a real event or private document. It does not search the web.

## Request and data flow

```text
PDF → page-aware chunks → OpenAI embeddings → FAISS + JSON metadata + hash manifest

Question → client admission → exact cache lookup
  ├─ hit: return saved answer and source references
  └─ miss: shared provider admission → query embedding → semantic cache lookup
       ├─ hit: reuse answer and original sources
       └─ miss: FAISS top-3 passages → OpenAI answer → citation check → cache
```

| Engineering choice | Mechanism |
| --- | --- |
| Shared cache | [`redis_cache.py`](phase2_retrieval/redis_cache.py) stores answers, vectors, source labels, expiry times, and bounded ordering in Upstash Redis. Lua updates perform insertion and eviction atomically. |
| Cache invalidation | [`resources.py`](phase2_retrieval/resources.py) derives the namespace from PDF, index and document-text/metadata hashes, embedding and answer models, threshold, and response-policy version. Changed citation metadata or the strict completion policy selects a new namespace, preventing stale cached answers from bypassing the updated context. |
| Admission before paid work | [`backend.py`](phase2_retrieval/backend.py) admits clients before lookup and uses a separate shared gate before query embedding. Exact hits avoid provider calls; semantic hits still require a query embedding. |
| Safe index loading | The loader checks corpus/index/metadata hashes and embedding dimensions, then reads FAISS plus JSON metadata rather than deserializing a pickle. |
| Answer boundary | Non-refusal answers require page labels present in the retrieved passages. Only a completed `stop` generation can enter the cache; truncated, filtered, tool-call and unknown completion states return explicit errors. |

Default cache settings are 256 entries and a 24-hour TTL per namespace. Semantic matching uses a cosine-distance threshold, so similar wording can reuse an answer. Citation-label checks validate page membership, not factual entailment.

The local Valkey adapter uses the same bounded hash/Lua contract as the Redis adapter, with a cosine scan of the configured entry limit. It reuses the query vector supplied by the handler, supports exact lookups before embedding, and does not require a vector-search module. This is a small bounded cache, not an indexed ANN service. Switching from the previous BetterDB adapter starts a new cache key layout; persisted document indexes remain unchanged. The legacy BetterDB package remains pinned in the dependency file but is no longer imported by the request path.

## Run locally

Use Python 3.12. From the repository root:

```powershell
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

On macOS/Linux, use `source .venv/bin/activate` and `cp .env.example .env`. Configure the untracked `.env`:

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | Server-side embedding and generation credential. |
| `LLM_MODEL`, `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | Defaults: `gpt-4o-mini`, `text-embedding-3-small`. Re-ingest when the embedding model changes. |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` | Redis admission credentials; also required for `CACHE_BACKEND=redis`. |
| `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED` | Defaults to `true`; invalid or unavailable Redis blocks admission. |
| `CACHE_BACKEND` | `local`, `valkey`, `auto`, or `redis`. `auto` tries Valkey and falls back to local SQLite; Vercel requires `redis`. |
| `CACHE_THRESHOLD`, `CACHE_TTL_SECONDS`, `CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES` | Defaults: `0.15`, `86400`, and `256`. |

The remaining timeout, request-budget, and Valkey options are in [`.env.example`](.env.example). For a local run without Redis, explicitly set `CACHE_BACKEND=local` and `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false`; this disables shared admission rather than simulating it.

Create the included contact-free sample, then build the index:

```powershell
python scripts/create_sample_pdf.py
python -m phase1_ingestion.ingest
python -m uvicorn phase2_retrieval.backend:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --no-proxy-headers
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000> for the browser UI. In a second terminal, `python -m streamlit run phase2_retrieval/frontend.py --server.port 8502` starts the alternate local interface. `BACKEND_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

For your own document, put an appropriate PDF at `data/symposium.pdf` before ingestion. The sample script refuses to overwrite an existing file. Ingestion sends extracted text to the configured embedding provider; PDFs, extracted data, indexes, local caches, and credentials are excluded from Git. Rebuild the index after changing the PDF or embedding model.

Windows shortcuts: `./run.ps1 ingest`, `./run.ps1 backend`, `./run.ps1 frontend`, and `./run.ps1 test` use the repository's `.venv`.

## Tests and verification

```powershell
python -m pytest -q
python -m pip check
python -m compileall -q config.py app.py phase1_ingestion phase2_retrieval scripts tests
```

The offline suite covers cache reuse and misses, eviction and TTL, Redis cache behavior, source preservation, refusal/citation handling, index validation, rate denial, and hosting configuration. [GitHub Actions](.github/workflows/tests.yml) runs the regression suite on Python 3.12 without a paid provider request.

With the included fictional sample indexed, OpenAI and Redis configured, and `RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=true` (restart the backend after configuration changes):

```powershell
python scripts/verify_live.py --url http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

This makes real embedding/generation requests, exercises cache behavior and HTTP errors, and uses isolated expiring Redis counters to check atomic admission and recovery. It writes a local verification report and consumes provider quota.

The [20 October hosted report](evidence/vercel-verification-report.md) records observed provider, cache, citation, and denial checks. It reports a one-page, one-chunk public sample; that demonstration does not establish retrieval quality for a larger corpus. No cost-savings or throughput figure is claimed.

## Workload and recovery measurements

The [benchmark guide](benchmarks/README.md) contains reproducible commands and retained reports. A local SQLite workload completed **9,000 operations** across three trials at concurrency 1, 4 and 8 with zero operation errors or expected-result mismatches. Four workers outperformed eight on this machine, so the report retains the contention tradeoff rather than claiming linear scaling.

The workload exposed unclosed SQLite handles; explicit connection closure now preserves transactions and rollback, with regression tests. Six adapter recovery checks and 18 isolated HTTP observations cover TTL refill, bounded eviction, writer contention, unavailable dependencies and recovery. The HTTP drill uses injected providers. A separate **real Redis drill** used 15 commands against isolated expiring keys: exactly three of 12 concurrent attempts were admitted, identities remained separate, and admission resumed after expiry. These are controlled development measurements, separate from the hosted Redis cache and production traffic.

## Deployment and limits

The [deployment guide](docs/vercel-deployment.md) explains the Vercel build and shared Redis cache. The build generates a fictional sample under `deploy_data/`, keeping original documents and local runtime data out of the upload. Streamlit remains a separate local interface.

Semantic cache reuse is heuristic and can conflate nearby intents. The cache performs a bounded vector scan rather than a distributed vector-index query. Request budgets limit request counts, not total provider spending; production use would need corpus-specific evaluation, traffic-aware budgeting, and monitoring.

# Apna Video Call

A full-stack video meeting app with peer-to-peer WebRTC media, shared PostgreSQL-backed signaling and room state, and guest or authenticated entry.

[Open the app](https://zoom-clone-blue-pi.vercel.app/) · [Meeting server](server/app.js) · [Media lifecycle](frontend/src/useMeeting.js) · [Integration tests](tests/integration.test.js)

## Features

- Start or join a meeting as a guest, or create an account and sign in.
- Invite others with a meeting link or room code.
- Make video and audio calls, mute your microphone, and turn your camera on or off.
- Share your screen and send messages in the meeting chat.
- Draw together on a shared whiteboard.
- Raise your hand, send emoji reactions, and see who is in the meeting.
- Record a selected screen or tab and download the video to your device.
- View your meeting history when signed in.

Meetings support up to **six people**. Anyone with the meeting link can join; rooms do not have an approval lobby or password.

## Architecture

```text
React / Vite browser clients
  ├─ Camera, microphone and screen → WebRTC peer connections
  ├─ Sign-in and history → Express HTTP API
  └─ Signaling, chat, reactions and whiteboard → Socket.IO
                                                 ↓
                                  PostgreSQL Socket.IO adapter
                                  Sessions, messages and presence
```

Media travels between peers, rather than through an application media server. The server coordinates room membership and SDP/ICE exchange. PostgreSQL shares signaling between server instances and persists accounts, rotating sessions, meeting history, chat and expiring participant leases.

| Engineering decision | Why it is there |
|---|---|
| Transactional room admission | A PostgreSQL advisory lock serializes joins to the same room before enforcing the six-participant cap. |
| One room per socket | Admission is reserved before the first asynchronous operation. Overlapping join requests cannot subscribe one socket to multiple rooms; failed database commits or adapter joins clear room privileges and subscriptions. |
| Expiring participant leases | Reconnect replaces the tab's previous lease; heartbeats refresh presence and stale leases expire after an interrupted process. |
| Room-scoped signaling | The server checks that signal recipients belong to the sender's room and bounds message sizes and event rates. |
| Hashed, rotating sessions | Access and refresh tokens are stored as hashes. Refresh replaces both tokens; logout revokes the stored session. |
| Authentication-rate identity | Direct deployments use the connection's peer address, ignoring client-supplied forwarding headers. Vercel deployments accept only a valid IP from the platform's `x-vercel-forwarded-for` header. |
| Explicit media cleanup | Peer connections and media tracks are stopped on exit; screen replacement and reconnect negotiation live in the shared meeting hook. |

The active implementation is [`server/`](server/) and [`frontend/`](frontend/). [`backend/`](backend/) contains the earlier implementation and is not the root application's runtime.

## Stack

React, Vite, Material UI, WebRTC, MediaRecorder, Express, Socket.IO, PostgreSQL, bcrypt, Node's test runner and Vitest.

## Run locally

Use **Node.js 22.x** and a dedicated PostgreSQL database. The PostgreSQL connection must support `LISTEN/NOTIFY`; use a direct connection rather than a transaction pooler.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/harshgavandit/Zoom_Clone.git
cd Zoom_Clone
npm ci
npm ci --prefix frontend
Copy-Item .env.example .env.local
```

Set `DATABASE_URL` and, when using a pooled provider URL, `DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED` in `.env.local`. The application prefers the unpooled URL. Schema tables are created on first readiness, so use an empty development database. `PORT` defaults to `8000`.

```powershell
# Terminal 1: HTTP API and signaling
npm start

# Terminal 2: Vite UI, with /api proxied to localhost:8000
npm --prefix frontend start
```

Open Vite's displayed local URL. For a single-origin production-style local run:

```powershell
npm run build
npm start
```

The server serves the built frontend at `http://localhost:8000`.

## Verification

```powershell
npm run check
npm --prefix frontend test
npm test
npm run build
```

`npm test` launches two local server instances against the configured PostgreSQL database and exercises authentication, refresh replay, logout revocation, room events and cross-room isolation. It creates synthetic accounts and meeting records; use a separate test database. Test ports `8121` and `8122` must be free.

The same command runs [admission-boundary regressions](tests/admission-boundaries.test.js) against the production connection handler with deterministic database/adapter failures, and [compressed-body checks](tests/compressed-body.test.js) against the installed HTTP middleware. These checks cover concurrent joins, failed-admission cleanup and spoofed forwarding headers. The two-instance suite verifies signaling and shared state; it does not measure real camera/audio quality or performance across different networks.

[CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml) supplies isolated PostgreSQL, runs frontend route tests and the two-instance integration suite, builds the UI and audits active dependencies. [`scripts/smoke.mjs`](scripts/smoke.mjs) contains the shared checks. `npm run test:live` defaults to `http://localhost:8000`; set `BASE_URL` and optionally `SECONDARY_URL` to test another deployment. It creates test accounts and meeting records, so use a dedicated environment and run it deliberately.

CI also checks the historical `backend/` dependencies separately with `npm ci --prefix backend --ignore-scripts`, `npm --prefix backend test`, and `npm audit --prefix backend --audit-level=moderate`. These offline checks exercise native bcrypt compatibility, Mongoose validation, existing authentication controllers and compressed-body parsing without connecting MongoDB or starting mediasoup workers. They do not replace a full SFU deployment test.

## Deployment and limits

[`vercel.json`](vercel.json) builds the Vite frontend and routes API/signaling traffic through [`api/index.js`](api/index.js). Configure the database URLs in the hosting environment. No database credential is sent to the browser.

- This is a small-group peer mesh, not an SFU. Browser bandwidth and CPU usage grow as more peers join.
- STUN is configured by default. Restricted networks may need an authenticated TURN relay via `TURN_URL`, `TURN_USERNAME` and `TURN_CREDENTIAL`; Vercel does not provide that relay.
- Camera and microphone access require browser permission and HTTPS, or localhost during development.
- Recordings stay on the user's device. The Recordings page lists downloads in the current browser; the files are saved in Downloads. There is no server-side recording archive.
- Guest rooms are accessible to anyone holding the link. This implementation does not claim enterprise meeting access controls or a production availability guarantee.

## Repository map

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `server/` | Active Express API, PostgreSQL state and Socket.IO coordination |
| `frontend/src/` | React pages, meeting hook, media controls and UI |
| `api/` | Vercel entry point |
| `tests/`, `scripts/smoke.mjs` | Two-instance API and signaling checks |
| `.github/workflows/` | PostgreSQL-backed CI |

# आगरी समाज · Agri Samaj

A Marathi-English community platform for discovering local businesses, sharing publications and events, and managing business registrations. This is community work, developed around the Agri Samaj community's requirements.

[Visit the website](https://agri-samaj-community-platform.vercel.app) · [Application routes](src/app) · [Database schema](prisma/schema.prisma) · [CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml)

![Agri Samaj community homepage](docs/images/community-homepage.png)

## What the platform does

- **Community discovery:** Marathi-English pages about Agri history, language, culture, organisations and initiatives, with links to official education, scholarship, employment and entrepreneurship resources.
- **Business directory:** Search by name, category, district or business type. Open public profiles, share search filters as URLs and save businesses to a private account shortlist.
- **News and publications:** Search published updates, browse upcoming or past events, download event calendar files and open community publication PDFs.
- **Business registration:** Create an account, save an application draft, attach supporting documents and track its review. Only approved businesses appear in public search.
- **Advertisements:** Choose a package, submit artwork and a payment reference, and follow an administrator-reviewed booking process.
- **Administration:** Review applications, request changes, approve or reject listings, manage categories, review advertisements and payment references, publish content, and handle inquiries.
- **Bilingual assistance:** Ask questions in Marathi or English, review recorded-question transcripts, read source-linked answers and listen to generated voice replies.

## Architecture

```text
Next.js / React interface
  ├─ Server-rendered public pages → bounded directory and community queries
  ├─ Member routes → session validation → owned business drafts and uploads
  ├─ Admin routes → role checks → review decisions and audit records
  └─ Assistant routes → persistent admission → public context → OpenAI
                                   ↓
                         Prisma / PostgreSQL
                  Private files: Vercel Blob or local storage
```

| Engineering decision | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Separate public and private records | Public queries select approved records; draft documents and owner fields have separate access checks. |
| Enforce ownership on the server | Business mutations validate the account and uploaded-file ownership before storing profile and audit changes in a transaction. |
| Recheck account state | JWT verification checks algorithm, issuer, audience and expiration; authenticated requests also load the active account and role. |
| Bound reads and shared traffic | Directory and admin queries use bounded pagination; PostgreSQL-backed counters enforce limits across application instances. |
| Keep AI within the website's scope | Context comes from public content and approved listings. Returned source identifiers are checked against the retrieved set. The assistant cannot read private applications or execute account actions. |
| Control generated voice | Voice replies require a signed, expiring token for a generated answer; provider calls receive cancellation signals and timeouts. |

See [authentication](src/lib/auth.ts), [business registration](src/app/api/businesses/register/route.ts), [request validation and limits](src/lib/http.ts), [assistant admission](src/lib/assistant-admission.ts), and [assistant source validation](src/app/api/assistant/chat/route.ts).

## Stack

Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Zod, bcrypt, JWT sessions, private Vercel Blob storage, OpenAI, Playwright and Node's test runner.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 22.x and a PostgreSQL database dedicated to this application.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/harshgavandit/agri-samaj-community-platform.git
cd agri-samaj-community-platform
npm ci
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

Configure `.env` before continuing:

| Variables | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `DATABASE_URL`, `DIRECT_URL` | PostgreSQL runtime and migration connections. Remote connections must require TLS. |
| `JWT_SECRET` | A unique cryptographically random secret of at least 32 characters. |
| `APP_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` | `http://localhost:3000` locally; the HTTPS origin when hosted. |
| `ADMIN_EMAIL`, `ADMIN_PASSWORD`, `ADMIN_NAME` | Administrator details for seeding. Use a unique password of at least 12 characters and at most 72 UTF-8 bytes. Existing accounts are not overwritten. |
| `UPLOAD_DIR` | Optional private durable directory for local uploads, outside `public/`. |
| `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` | Private Blob store on Vercel; keep it server-side. |

```powershell
npm run check:env
npm run prisma:generate
npm run db:deploy
npm run prisma:seed
npm run dev
```

Migrations and seeding write to the configured application database. Use a local development database. Open `http://localhost:3000`.

The assistant is optional. Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `OPENAI_MODEL` to enable it. Voice settings are `OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and `OPENAI_VOICE_MODEL`; `ASSISTANT_HOURLY_LIMIT` bounds shared provider operations. Other website features do not require a provider key. See [`.env.example`](.env.example) for the complete variable list.

## Verification

```powershell
npm run lint
npm run type-check
npm test
npm run build
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

Browser tests need a dedicated **local** PostgreSQL server. Set `E2E_DATABASE_URL` if the default `127.0.0.1:5547/agri_test` is unavailable. The runner creates an isolated schema and synthetic fixtures; never point tests at the deployed application database. Normal tests disable provider calls. Live AI and Blob checks are explicit opt-ins in [the runner](tests/run-e2e.mjs).

[CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml) starts PostgreSQL and runs lint, type checks, unit tests, dependency audit, production build and browser journeys. Regressions cover registration/upload ownership, withdrawn-image privacy, directory filtering, private shortlists, admin pagination, session validation, request bounds and assistant controls.

## Operational scope

- Business and advertisement publication requires administrator review. Advertisement payment references are reviewed manually; this is not an automated payment processor.
- The assistant uses published website content. It has no live web search and cannot approve applications, verify payments or change accounts.
- The community's administrators determine content and roadmap. No official government endorsement, adoption metric or production service-level guarantee is implied.
- On Vercel, use PostgreSQL and a **private** Blob store. Local filesystem uploads require durable private storage when self-hosting.

## Repository map

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/app/` | Public pages, member/admin interfaces and API routes |
| `src/lib/` | Auth, validation, public data, storage and AI boundaries |
| `prisma/` | PostgreSQL schema, migrations and controlled seed data |
| `tests/` | Unit, security and Playwright regression tests |

# Architecture and data guarantees

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> E[Nginx local / TLS ALB cloud]
  E --> A[Independent Express replicas]
  A --> M[(Mongo primary)]
  A --> R[(Rebuildable Redis catalog cache)]
  M --> O[Leased outbox relay]
  O --> Q[SQS / local ElasticMQ]
  Q --> W[Independent bounded workers]
  W --> M
  Q --> D[Dead-letter queue]
  A --> T[OpenTelemetry collector]
  W --> T
  O --> T
  A --> P[Direct Prometheus scrapes]
  E --> L[Bounded edge/log receiver]
  L --> G[Grafana: metrics, logs, traces]
  P --> G
  T --> G
```

Protected requests verify authoritative Mongo sessions and account state through bounded linearizable primary reads. Independent session/account reads run concurrently; both must finish successfully before authorization, quota writes or mutations. Redis cannot authorize a revoked session. Requests already authorized before a completed revocation may finish. Refresh tokens are stored as hashes and rotate through an atomic compare-and-set; a replay or concurrent loser revokes the family and requires sign-in.

Product changes require a server-side administrator role. Cart, wishlist and job access are scoped to the authenticated owner. Mutations store an idempotency receipt and their effects in one majority transaction. A retry with the same key and input returns the saved response; changed input returns 409. Cart increments and guarded deletes retry transaction conflicts rather than lose committed increments.

Ingestion returns 202 only after a majority transaction commits the job, idempotency scope and outbox event. A leased relay publishes a versioned message and can publish twice after a crash. Workers commit the product effect and terminal state before acknowledging the message. Duplicate transport produces one logical effect. This is at-least-once transport with idempotent effects. Failed jobs are isolated after bounded attempts; redrive is an audited generation change.

Redis holds public catalog responses for at most 30 seconds from read start, with downward jitter, namespace invalidation, bounded payloads and per-process single-flight. Authorization/cookie requests bypass caching. A Redis outage uses a bounded Mongo fallback; overload is a visible 503. Nginx caching is disabled. Stock and payments are outside this catalog lab's acceptance contract.

The local environment has one Mongo member and one host. Separate containers prove process/replica behavior, not independent fault domains. Cloud IaC describes private ECS services, TLS ALB, WAF, encrypted Redis/SQS, private Atlas connectivity, separate runtime/migration identities and managed telemetry. That architecture remains undeployed while cloud configuration is absent.

Local gateway stale-address connection attempts are bounded to 250 milliseconds, with up to four upstream attempts within a four-second total retry budget. Writes retain the default non-idempotent replay protection described in the [NGINX proxy retry documentation](https://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_proxy_module.html#proxy_next_upstream). Edge diagnostics retain upstream address/status/connect time without request bodies, query strings or authorization headers. A repeated three-cycle stop/restart test checks actual content and zero failures at 100 catalog requests/s; the report is separate from mixed-workload capacity.

## Configuration and boundaries

The serving container starts compiled code directly as a non-root user with a read-only root filesystem and bounded temporary space. The vertical entrypoint starts four workers in one 4 CPU/4 GiB container. Horizontal uses four 1 CPU/1 GiB API containers. Relay/worker pools, concurrency and queue leases are independent of API replicas. Mongo remains the authority across all of them.

Runtime source identity is recorded in an OCI image label. CI exports and hashes the tested image archive; security checks scan that archive; publication verifies identity, durability, scan and operational evidence before signing the registry digest. Production promotes the same tested digest and requires real staging business and SLO evidence.

# ADR 0001: Canonical Express service and durable effects

Status: accepted for implementation, cloud operation pending.

The five-framework lab needs a comparable contract while production hardening requires one operational target. Express is canonical. Comparison backends advertise their actual capabilities; missing Go routes are not silently treated as passing. The historical vertical exercise stays separate from the horizontal profile.

Mongo is the durable authority for sessions, idempotency receipts, ingestion jobs and outbox. Majority transactions connect acknowledgement to persisted work. SQS provides at-least-once delivery; leased workers and unique transactional effects tolerate duplicates. Redis is rebuildable public-catalog acceleration. Private authorization never depends on positive Redis cache entries.

ECS/Atlas are the cloud reference because separate tasks, managed data and protected digest promotion meet the scope without adding a Kubernetes control plane. This choice adds provider/network/state/secret operational work. Local Compose supplies repeatable failure tests but cannot establish cloud AZ or PIT recovery.

Tradeoffs: authoritative session reads add database latency; a 30-second catalog TTL permits explicitly bounded staleness; refresh races require reauthentication; Mongo remains a shared bottleneck. Raise pools, replicas or introduce new data infrastructure only after measured capacity identifies a constraint and the cost/consistency model is documented.
